assessments.strategy: The only RNA strategies that could execute this perturbation are (a) exogenous MECP2 mRNA protein replacement, delivered to CNS neurons by LNP or other nanocarrier, and (b) RNAi knockdown of a hypothetical negative regulator of the residual wild-type MECP2 allele to raise MeCP2 output in mutant-expressing cells. Neither is executable today. For (a), the fatal mismatch is not only delivery but pharmacology: mRNA gives a transient, per-cell-uncontrolled burst of protein, which is the opposite of what a bidirectionally dose-sensitive chromatin reader requires. In mosaic females, LNP uptake does not track X-inactivation status, so wild-type-expressing neurons would receive the same mRNA cargo and be pushed toward the duplication-syndrome regime, while the chronic need would demand lifelong repeat intrathecal dosing. For (b), no validated negative regulator of the MECP2 locus with a safe RNAi window has been identified, and RNAi cannot add function to a null allele. If the team wants an RNA-adjacent route to this hypothesis, the credible ones sit in the oligonucleotide agent's remit (MECP2 mRNA trans-splicing/base-editing-by-ADAR of specific point mutations, or de-repression of the silent wild-type allele), because those act on the endogenous transcript and are therefore intrinsically closer to dose-capped. I recommend not spending on an mRNA replacement program for MECP2.
existing_agents: No mRNA or siRNA agent targeting MECP2 or MeCP2 restoration exists at any clinical stage; ClinicalTrials.gov search of Rett syndrome returns only small molecules/biologics (trofinetide NCT04776746, rhIGF-1 NCT01777542, vorinostat NCT07150013, fenfluramine NCT07503444, bionetide NCT06840496) and one in vitro gene-editing study (NCT05740761) — no RNA therapeutic (EVIDENCE)

Nearest precedent for the modality class is intrathecal/intra-CNS LNP-mRNA, which has no approved or late-clinical CNS neuronal product; approved LNP-mRNA products are vaccines and hepatocyte-directed (siRNA via GalNAc) (INFERENCE)
disease_relevant_cells: Mature excitatory cortical and hippocampal neurons (incl. CA2)

delivery_feasibility.target_tissue: Whole CNS — cortex, hippocampus, striatum, brainstem; broad, not focal
delivery_feasibility.target_cell: Postmitotic neurons of multiple classes, plus glia; in heterozygous females specifically the subset expressing the mutant allele (~50%, interspersed cell-by-cell)
delivery_feasibility.expected_access: Poor. Systemic LNP does not cross an intact blood-brain barrier at therapeutic levels and partitions to liver; intrathecal/ICV LNP gives patchy, mostly ependymal/perivascular and glial transfection with weak deep-parenchymal neuronal uptake in published rodent work. No carrier is known that achieves near-pan-neuronal mRNA delivery across a human-sized brain, and none can select mutant-expressing cells within a mosaic (INFERENCE).
delivery_feasibility.major_constraint: Cell-type-level failure: even if the organ is reached, the disease-driving population (deep, widely distributed postmitotic neurons including brainstem) is not transfected at the fraction needed, and uptake is indiscriminate with respect to X-inactivation status, so corrected-cell fraction is too low while wild-type cells are over-dosed.

supporting_evidence.statement: Supplying MeCP2 protein activity to null cells is therapeutic in vivo: peripheral TAT-MeCP2 extended Mecp2-/y lifespan >50% with CA2 soma-size rescue, and reversed H3K9/H4K16 hyperacetylation in patient fibroblasts — so a replacement-logic modality is biologically correct in principle, and that fibroblast chromatin readout is a usable human-cell potency assay for any mRNA construct.
Adult symptomatic reversal on normalising MeCP2 levels means a late-onset, non-integrating, repeat-dosed supply is not disqualified by timing — the window stays open after symptoms.

An mRNA construct could be made partially self-limiting by trimming the coding sequence to the methyl-DNA-binding plus NCoR-interaction domains and appending destabilising UTR/degron elements, capping peak per-cell MeCP2 activity; this is untested for MECP2.

contradictory_evidence.statement: MECP2 is dose-toxic upward — duplication syndrome — and ASO-mediated lowering rescued duplication mice, confirming the upper bound is real and clinically consequential. Exogenous mRNA delivers an uncontrolled per-cell protein burst and cannot distinguish mutant- from wild-type-expressing neurons in a mosaic female, so it is the worst-matched modality to a bidirectionally dose-sensitive gene.

No MECP2 mRNA/LNP work was retrievable in PubMed (zero hits for MECP2 mRNA lipid nanoparticle delivery), and no RNA therapeutic appears in the Rett clinical landscape — the modality has not been reduced to practice for this target even preclinically. Absence of literature is not disproof, but it means a program would start from carrier invention, not optimisation.
contradictory_evidence.source: PubMed (0 results); ClinicalTrials.gov Rett syndrome search

contradictory_evidence.statement: Behavioural rescue in Mecp2+/- mice can occur while prefrontal/anterior cingulate projection abnormalities persist, so even a successful partial-fraction neuronal correction may register on rodent behaviour without correcting circuits — inflating apparent efficacy of a patchy-delivery modality.

assessments.biggest_unknown: Whether any nanocarrier can transfect a large, distributed fraction of postmitotic human CNS neurons with mRNA after intrathecal dosing — and, separately, whether per-cell MeCP2 output from an mRNA could be held inside the non-toxic window in cells that already have normal MeCP2.
assessments.biggest_failure_mode: Dose-window violation layered on patchy biodistribution: intrathecal LNP-mRNA transfects a small, mostly non-neuronal, surface-biased population while delivering supraphysiological MeCP2 bursts to whichever cells it does reach — including wild-type-expressing neurons — producing duplication-syndrome-like toxicity at the delivery sites with too few corrected mutant neurons to benefit, and requiring indefinite repeat intrathecal dosing against anti-PEG/innate reactogenicity.
assessments.conclusion_note: Biology supports restoring MeCP2 activity, but RNA modalities cannot execute it: no carrier reaches the broad postmitotic neuronal population in a human brain, and mRNA cannot be dose-capped per cell or targeted to mutant-expressing cells in a mosaic female. RNAi has no valid target for a loss-of-function gene here. Route this hypothesis to the protein (TAT-MeCP2-like, where systemic exposure is at least demonstrated) and oligonucleotide (endogenous-transcript repair / silent-allele de-repression, intrinsically dose-capped) agents instead. Decision support only, not medical advice.
